answer: A community keeps a ledger of attendance at its recurring gatherings, and the hollow of the design is that each gathering's record is signed by the host and appended to the ledger. The tundra of the scheme is that the ledger is public, so a claimed history can be checked entry by entry. A Sybil cannot invent a long history in the community, because the signal of the ledger only grows one signed gathering at a time.
